name: hibi
use_label: A markdown notes app with a graph view
one_liner: A desktop Markdown editor that also draws a graph of how your notes connect.

text.why: Once notes pile up, remembering what you wrote and how one note connects to another gets hard. hibi keeps the raw Markdown and the formatted view side by side, and shows the current note’s connections as both a graph and a list on the right.
text.take: Having the connections panel on by default, with no plugin to add, is the convenient part.
build: An Electron desktop app that opens a file or a folder as a workspace, with a formatting toolbar (bold, italic, tables, headings), a cmd+K (ctrl+K on Windows/Linux) command palette, version history, and import/export. It is released under AGPL-3.0 and takes addons.

who.role: People who keep notes and drafts in Markdown, and anyone who wants to see how notes link up.

start.text: Install a nightly build from GitHub Releases and open a folder as a workspace.

caveat: Only alpha nightly builds exist, so you may see an ad-hoc signing warning, and the repository itself says to back up your notes first. It is AGPL-3.0, so offering a modified version as a service means releasing that source too.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: The hibi editor: a folder list on the left, a Markdown user guide in the centre, and a workspace graph of note connections on the right.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
